newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: DEATH LINKED TO HOSPITAL FOOD POISONING
An elderly woman has died from salmonella poisoning sourced to food served at Brisbane's Mater Hospital.
The 92-year old had been a patient at the hospital for an unrelated procedure when she was diagnosed with salmonella poisoning last week.
There've been 27 confirmed cases of salmonella in the hospital, most of them in the Mater Mothers and among training staff.
A hospital spokeswoman says most of those affected have recovered from the salmonella poisoning.
BEAZLEY SAYS GOVERNMENT LACKS CONSCIENCE ON ENVIRONMENT
Federal Opposition leader, Kim Beazley, says the government has demonstrated a lack of conscience over plans to allow mining in some forest areas.
Mining will be allowed in informal reserves, which are classified as less environmentally important than dedicated reserves.
But subject to Commonwealth approval, the states WILL be allowed to permit mining in dedicated reserves.
Mr Beazley says it's clear the government is not to be trusted over environmental matters
ACOSS SAYS BURDEN ON LOW INCOME EARNERS
The Australian Council of Social Service has asked the Industrial Relations Commission to deliver low income earners a wage rise equal to growth in average weekly earnings.
ACOSS has delivered its submission to the Commission's hearing into the ACTU's Living Wage Claim in Sydney.
The Reserve Bank's monthly bulletin says if the ACTU's eight-and-three-quarter per cent claim is paid, wages growth will go beyond five per cent.
But ACOSS has accused the Reserve Bank of trying to force all the burden of wage restraint onto low income earners.
HOPES OF GREATER STABILITY IN WOOL MARKET
The Federal Government says a 300 million dollar export credit facility for Chinese importers of Australian wool has the potential to make a significant impact on the Australian industry.
The facility, set up by the Commonwealth Bank, will mean Chinese importers can get up to 180 days of credit.
The industry believes it will maintain and stabilise what has been a volatile market, while giving the potential to expand trade.
China is Australia's largest wool market, taking 26 per cent of production.
ALSTON CALLS ON PEOPLE TO BUY DIGITAL PHONES
Federal Communications Minister, Richard Alston, has called on people buying mobile phones for Christmas to make it a digital phone.
Analogue phone services are being phased out in favor of digitals over the next three years.
Senator Alston says it's time to make the switch to digital, which offers better voice quality, security and more features.
